arxiv-2103-00747.title: Combat COVID-19 Infodemic Using Explainable Natural Language Processing Models Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2103-00747.creator: Jackie Ayoub, X. Jessie Yang, Feng Zhou, Manuscript accepted by Information Processing and Management
arxiv-2103-00747.description: Abstract Misinformation of COVID-19 is prevalent on social media as the pandemic unfolds, and the associated risks are extremely high. Thus, it is critical to detect and combat such misinformation. Recently, deep learning models using natural language processing techniques, such as BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers), have achieved great successes in detecting misinformation.

arxiv-2103-08444.title: Energy Conditions in f ⁡ ( P ) f(P) Gravity
arxiv-2103-08444.creator: Snehasish Bhattacharjee
arxiv-2103-08444.description: Abstract f ⁡ ( P ) f(P) gravity is a novel extension of ECG in which the Ricci scalar in the action is replaced by a function of the curvature invariant P P which represents the contractions of the Riemann tensor at the cubic order p .

arxiv-2107-02125.title: Characterization of multiframelet set on local fields of positive characteristic
arxiv-2107-02125.creator: Debasis Haldar
arxiv-2107-02125.description: Abstract . This paper presents a discussion on multiframelet set, multiwavelet set and set correspond to super wavelet on local fields of positive characteristic. We characterize Parseval multiframelet set and give equivalent conditions multiwavelet set holds. Furthurmore, we characterize MRA multiwavelet set with the help of dimension function. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 42C15, 43A70; Secondary 42C40 1.

arxiv-2208-11976.title: A statistical test of market efficiency based on information theory
arxiv-2208-11976.creator: Xavier Brouty, Matthieu Garcin
arxiv-2208-11976.description: Abstract We determine the amount of information contained in a time series of price returns at a given time scale, by using a widespread tool of the information theory, namely the Shannon entropy, applied to a symbolic representation of this time series.

arxiv-2212-07668.title: BPS Lie algebras for totally negative 2 2 -Calabi–Yau categories and nonabelian Hodge theory for stacks
arxiv-2212-07668.creator: Ben Davison, Lucien Hennecart, Sebastian Schlegel Mejia
arxiv-2212-07668.description: Abstract . We define and study a sheaf-theoretic cohomological Hall algebra for suitably geometric Abelian categories 𝒜 \mathcal{A} of homological dimension at most two, and a sheaf-theoretic BPS algebra under the conditions that 𝒜 \mathcal{A} is 2-Calabi–Yau and has a good moduli space.

arxiv-2401-17937.title: Branch and Price for the Length-Constrained Cycle Partition Problem
arxiv-2401-17937.creator: Mohammed Ghannam, Gioni Mexi, Edward Lam, Ambros Gleixner
arxiv-2401-17937.description: Abstract The length-constrained cycle partition problem (LCCP) is a graph optimization problem in which a set of nodes must be partitioned into a minimum number of cycles. Every node is associated with a critical time and the length of every cycle must not exceed the critical time of any node in the cycle.

arxiv-2403-15762.title: RicMonk: A Three-Link Brachiation Robot with Passive Grippers for Energy-Efficient Brachiation
arxiv-2403-15762.creator: Shourie S. Grama, Mahdi Javadi, Shivesh Kumar, Hossein Zamani Boroujeni, Frank Kirchner
arxiv-2403-15762.description: Abstract This paper presents the design, analysis, and performance evaluation of RicMonk, a novel three-link brachiation robot equipped with passive hook-shaped grippers. Brachiation, an agile and energy-efficient mode of locomotion observed in primates, has inspired the development of RicMonk to explore versatile locomotion and maneuvers on ladder-like structures.

arxiv-2406-10759.title: Humanoid Parkour Learning
arxiv-2406-10759.creator: Ziwen Zhuang, Shenzhe Yao, Hang Zhao
arxiv-2406-10759.description: Abstract Parkour is a grand challenge for legged locomotion, even for quadruped robots, requiring active perception and various maneuvers to overcome multiple challenging obstacles. Existing methods for humanoid locomotion either optimize a trajectory for a single parkour track or train a reinforcement learning policy only to walk with a significant amount of motion references.

arxiv-2410-18202.title: PyTSC: A Unified Platform for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning in Traffic Signal Control
arxiv-2410-18202.creator: Rohit Bokade, Xiaoning Jin
arxiv-2410-18202.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rohit Bokade, Xiaoning Jin. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) presents a promising approach for addressing the complexity of Traffic Signal Control (TSC) in urban environments. However, existing platforms for MARL-based TSC research face challenges such as slow simulation speeds and convoluted, difficult-to-maintain codebases. To address these limitations, we introduce PyTSC, a robust and flexible simulation environment that facilitates the training and evaluation of MARL algorithms for TSC.

arxiv-2504-18150.description: Abstract . Docker has gained attention as a lightweight container-based virtualization platform. The process for building a Docker image is defined in a text file called a Dockerfile. A Dockerfile can be considered as a kind of source code that contains instructions on how to build a Docker image.

arxiv-2509-13547.title: AI Agents with Human-Like Collaborative Tools: Adaptive Strategies for Enhanced Problem-Solving
arxiv-2509-13547.creator: Harper Reed, Michael Sugimura, Angelo Zangari
arxiv-2509-13547.description: Abstract We investigate whether giving LLM agents the collaborative tools and autonomy that humans naturally use for problem-solving can improve their performance, providing Claude Code agents with MCP-based social media and journaling tools and the flexibility to use them as they see fit.

arxiv-2602-07825.title: Estimation Strategies for Causal Decomposition Analysis with Allowability Specifications
arxiv-2602-07825.creator: John W. Jackson, Ting-Hsuan Chang, Aster Meche, Trang Quynh Nguyen
arxiv-2602-07825.description: Abstract Causal decomposition analysis (CDA) is an approach for modeling the impact of hypothetical interventions to reduce disparities. It is useful for identifying foci that future interventions, including multilevel and multimodal interventions, could focus on to reduce disparities. Based within the potential outcomes framework, CDA has a causal interpretation when the identifying assumptions are met.

openalex-w2022905671.description: Most individuals throughout the Americas are admixed descendants of Native American, European, and African ancestors. Complex historical factors have resulted in varying proportions of ancestral contributions between individuals within and among ethnic groups. We developed a...

plos-pone-0004297.creator: Terence M. Murphy, Mark Belmonte, Stephanie Shu et al.
plos-pone-0004297.description: PLOS ONE research article. Arabidopsis thaliana has three genes, Ape1L , Ape2 , and Arp , that show homology to abasic (apurinic/apyrimidinic) endonuclease genes of bacterial, yeast, or animal cells. In bacteria, yeast, and animals, abasic endonucleases function in base excision repair of oxidized and othe

pmc-10604307.title: Correction of Arterial-Phase Motion Artifacts in Gadoxetic Acid-Enhanced Liver MRI Using an Innovative Unsupervised Network
pmc-10604307.creator: Feng Pan, Qianqian Fan, Han Xie, Chongxin Bai, Zhi Zhang, Hebing Chen, Lian Yang, Xin Zhou, Qingjia Bao, Chaoyang Liu
pmc-10604307.description: This study aims to propose and evaluate DR-CycleGAN, a disentangled unsupervised network by introducing a novel content-consistency loss, for removing arterial-phase motion artifacts in gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver MRI examinations. From June 2020 to July 2021, gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver MRI data were retrospectively collected in this center to establish training and testing datasets.

pmc-11654053.title: An intracranial odyssey: pediatric ganglioneuroma arising from the trigeminal ganglion: a case report and review of the literature
pmc-11654053.creator: Kaveh Ebrahimzadeh, Mohammad Mirahmadi Eraghi, Farahnaz Bidari Zerehpoosh, Hesameddin Hoseini Tavasol, Mahkameh Abbaszdeh, Adam A. Dmytriw, Fatemeh Jahanshahi
pmc-11654053.description: BackgroundGanglioneuroma represents an uncommon benign tumor arising from the sympathetic nerves, and its development from the fifth nerve is an infrequent entity. Few ganglioneuromas arising from the fifth nerve have been discussed in literature. The authors describe the second pediatric ganglioneuroma arising from the fifth nerve.

pmc-12444152.title: Association between tacrolimus blood levels and biopsy-proven acute cellular rejection in adult heart transplant recipients
pmc-12444152.creator: Chengliang Yang, Casey P Shannon, Sara Assadian, Linda Lapp, Rithika Nair, Tao Huan, Nilu Partovi, Mustafa Toma, Scott J Tebbutt
pmc-12444152.description: BackgroundAcute cellular rejection (ACR) is a common complication following heart transplantation (HTx). This study examined the association between tacrolimus whole-blood concentrations and endomyocardial biopsy (EMB)-proven ACR in adult HTx recipients.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective analysis of 41 adult HTx recipients enrolled in the HEARTBiT study at St. Paul’s Hospital (Vancouver, Canada) between August 2018 and February 2020.

pmc-12535735.title: Does Robotic Total Hip Arthroplasty Technology Have Any Benefit in Achieving Equal Limb Length via the Direct Anterior Approach?
pmc-12535735.creator: Mawardi B Mustapha, Agir Muzaffer, Javad Parvizi, Ibrahim Tuncay
pmc-12535735.description: BackgroundLeg length discrepancy (LLD) is a common and clinically significant complication following total hip arthroplasty (THA), potentially affecting functional outcomes and patient satisfaction. Robotic-assisted THA has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional techniques, offering enhanced precision in implant positioning.

pmc-12580182.title: The efficacy of lactic acid bacteria-based toothpaste on oral health: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12580182.creator: Eun-Mi Choi, Su-Kyung Park
pmc-12580182.description: IntroductionLactic acid bacteria (LAB) have emerged as promising adjunctive agents for oral health management due to their antimicrobial and immunomodulatory properties. With the increasing incorporation of probiotics into oral care products, it is critical to evaluate their clinical efficacy. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to assess the effectiveness of LAB-based toothpaste in improving oral health outcomes.

pmc-12654450.title: Beyond the Surface: Revealing the Concealed Effects of Hyperglycemia on Ocular Surface Homeostasis and Dry Eye Disease
pmc-12654450.creator: Marco Zeppieri, Matteo Capobianco, Federico Visalli, Mutali Musa, Alessandro Avitabile, Rosa Giglio, Daniele Tognetto, Caterina Gagliano, Fabiana D’Esposito, Francesco Cappellani, Andrzej Grzybowski, Stephen G Schwartz, Krishna S Kishor, Victor M Villegas, Christopher Leffler
pmc-12654450.description: Background and Objectives: Dry eye disease (DED) is a multifactorial ocular surface disease that markedly diminishes quality of life. Although diabetes mellitus is well-known for its retinal consequences, anterior segment symptoms including dry eye disease are often overlooked. Chronic hyperglycemia causes metabolic, neurovascular, and immunological changes that undermine tear film stability, corneal innervation, and ocular surface integrity.

pmc-12704539.title: Spiroplasma ixodetis in Ticks Removed from Humans, Sweden and Åland Islands, Finland
pmc-12704539.creator: Malin Lager, Yousif Alkattan, Amanda Sandbacka Karlsson, Louise Fernström, Anna Grankvist, Christine Wennerås, Marika Nordberg, Dag Nyman, Per-Eric Lindgren, Pia Forsberg, Peter Wilhelmsson, Anna J. Henningsson
pmc-12704539.description: The prevalence of Spiroplasma ixodetis in ticks that have bitten humans in Sweden and in the Åland Islands, Finland, was 2.6%, with observed significant geographic differences between regions. The pathogen was not detected in blood samples from participants bitten by S. ixodetis–positive ticks, indicating low risk for transmission to humans.

pmc-13017038.title: Intra-aneurysmal Thrombectomy Using Exo-endoscopic 2-step Approach for Thrombosed Vertebral Artery Aneurysm: A Technical Case Report
pmc-13017038.creator: I Gusti Ketut Agung Surya KENCANA, Kenichiro IWAMI, Masahiro NISHIHORI, Kazuhito TAKEUCHI, Yuichi NAGATA, Eriko OKUMURA, Yoshiki SATO, I Wayan NIRYANA, Tjokorda Gde Bagus MAHADEWA, Ryuta SAITO
pmc-13017038.description: Although rare, thrombosed vertebral artery aneurysms can lead to severe symptoms and are challenging to treat due to their proximity to vital structures. The location of a thrombosed aneurysm on the anterior aspect of the brainstem poses a significant challenge to conventional microscopic approaches.

pmc-13101579.title: Deceptive Lesion: When Benign Biopsies Mask a Massive Verrucous Carcinoma
pmc-13101579.creator: Monica Schouten, Marije M. van Santen, Liesbeth M. Kager
pmc-13101579.description: nancy. Pathology review at a tertiary center was inconclusive. Empiric antifungal therapy failed. Positron emission tomography–computed tomography subsequently showed a fluorodeoxyglucose–avid stenosing mass with regional lymphadenopathy, highly suspicious for esophageal carcinoma (Figure B). Despite these findings, the patient declined both chemoradiotherapy and surgical resection. Following transient clinical improvement, the patient died of an upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage.

pmc-13161735.title: Canine Urothelial DNA Mutations Are Not Associated With Total Trihalomethanes Concentrations in Municipal Drinking Water
pmc-13161735.creator: Janice O'Brien, Samantha L Braman, Jennifer Willcox, Phillip Wang, Daniel Gerrity, Audrey Ruple, Lauren A Trepanier
pmc-13161735.description: Contaminants in municipal drinking water, specifically total trihalomethanes (TTHMs), are mutagenic. Exposures to TTHMs have been associated with urothelial carcinoma (UC) in both people and dogs. Mutations in the BRAF gene and other genomic copy number aberrations detected in voided urothelial cells with commercial CADET BRAF and BRAF‐PLUS tests have also been associated with the presence of UC in dogs.

pmc-13393677.title: Multi-dimensional risk prediction and genetic architecture of aspiration pneumonia: a population-based analysis
pmc-13393677.creator: Chaoyuan Jin, Qingxia Dai, Xingxing Ren, Jie Shen
pmc-13393677.description: BackgroundAspiration pneumonia represents a significant but understudied cause of morbidity and mortality, particularly among aging populations with neurological comorbidities. Current risk stratification tools rely on single-dimensional clinical data, limiting their predictive accuracy and population health utility. This study aimed to develop comprehensive risk prediction models and identify genetic determinants of aspiration pneumonia using integrated epidemiological, computational, and genomic approaches.

pmc-13598447.title: Real-world outcomes for multiple myeloma patients after apheresis for planned chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy
pmc-13598447.creator: Ayrton Bangolo, Sarvarinder Gill, Lili Zhang, Jiahe Zhao, Behzad Amoozgar, Ronit Reich-Slotky, Justin Tran, Tri Vo, Gabby Mariblanca, Xenia Balulescu, Sean Mcknight, Nidhi Patel, Aidan Reed, Sukhmani Kaur, Shalini Subramanian, Julie Katyal, Christo Manikkuttiyil, Morgan Chakov, Alisa Nguyen, Sanjana
pmc-13598447.description: BACKGROUNDChimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy is highly active in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM), but manufacturing creates an obligatory waiting period between apheresis and infusion. Patients may deteriorate, progress or die during this window. Analyses that begin follow-up at infusion exclude these patients entirely and cannot describe the experience of all patients who enter the CAR-T pathway.

pmc-13607301.title: The Nonlinear Association Between Adipose Tissue Insulin Resistance and Remnant Cholesterol in Chinese Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13607301.creator: Ruixiang Cui, Honglin Sun, Mengge Yang, Ying Wang, Jia Liu, Guang Wang
pmc-13607301.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Adipose tissue insulin resistance (Adipo-IR) is a key driver in the pathogenesis of cardiometabolic diseases. Dyslipidemia, particularly elevated remnant cholesterol (RC), is also strongly associated with cardiometabolic risk and has been recognized as a highly atherogenic lipid marker. Although systemic IR is known to be linked to dyslipidemia and elevated RC, the specific relationship between Adipo-IR and RC remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the association between Adipo-IR and RC as well as its consistency across different subgroups.
